criteria.description: The result is one concise, creator-reviewable 60-second production specification grounded in the supplied screenplay. It does not become a source audit, generic workflow, production diary, or set of separate stage documents.
The specification establishes one coherent experience or narrative spine and only the cross-shot visual, action, sound, scope, and acceptance rules that downstream production must preserve.

Recurring character and scene continuity is explicit, source-grounded, limited to generation-critical properties, and distinguishes required preservation from forbidden drift without repeating one-off shot details.

One authoritative table gives stable production-unit identity and owns timing, story function, image and action, camera and sound, real input requirements, production method, direct acceptance, and downstream use without duplicating those decisions elsewhere.

One cross-unit contract gives applicable editorial, compositing, grade, sound, title or caption, master, and delivery-result constraints. Unknown measured or platform-specific parameters remain explicit dependencies rather than invented defaults.

The document contains no model call packet because execution was excluded, and it does not copy runtime status, candidate history, failures, project revisions, or export receipts into prose. Analysis remains outside the reusable specification.
